title: Jeremy Thomas
text:
Welcome to my website!
I’m a PhD researcher turned data scientist with 4+ years of experience analyzing high-frequency biometric and behavioral data, including eye-tracking and human motion.
My work focuses on quantitative modeling and prediction of human behavior, with an emphasis on translating messy experimental data into interpretable, decision-relevant models.
Across academic research and applied projects, I’ve developed strengths in experimental design, causal inference, statistical modeling, and rapid model prototyping, primarily using Python. I’m especially interested in problems where careful measurement and statistical thinking matter as much as raw scale.
This site highlights a selection of projects that reflect how I approach data: formulating precise questions, validating assumptions, and building models that are both rigorous and practical.

title: Projects
text:
Python · Classification · Regression

Built an end-to-end modeling pipeline to predict product adoption across 25,000+ merchants using 1.5M+ transaction-level time-series observations

Engineered temporal behavioral features from raw transactional data, including usage intensity, recency, and growth trends

Trained and evaluated logistic regression, random forest, and SVM classifiers using cross-validation

Demonstrated that a regularized logistic regression model matched the predictive performance of more complex classifiers while enabling clear, interpretable feature effects

Used value-based evaluation metrics to maximize business impact rather than pure predictive ability
Ranked the top 10–15% of merchants for targeted marketing and used model coefficients to identify the primary drivers of subscription adoption

What I’d do next

Model adoption timing using survival or hazard-based approaches rather than static classification

Validate targeting strategies via offline backtesting paired with online experimentation assumptions
GitHub Repository





Python · Experimentation · Unsupervised Learning · Dimensionality Reduction

Designed and analyzed a large-scale motor learning experiment (10,000+ trials) using high-resolution motion-tracking data

Applied clustering methods (k-means, HMMs) to uncover latent structure in learning trajectories

Quantified individual differences in adaptation strategies, moving beyond group-level averages

Emphasized robustness checks, sensitivity analyses, and interpretability of unsupervised results

What I’d do next

Incorporate hierarchical or Bayesian state-space models to better capture learning dynamics over time

Evaluate cluster stability using bootstrap or permutation-based methods

Extend the analysis to link inferred strategies with downstream performance or transfer effects





Statistical Modeling · Regression · Time Series

Modeled reaction time as a function of imposed rotation magnitude and task structure

Compared linear, nonlinear (splines), and piecewise regression models

Evaluated models using out-of-sample performance and interpretability criteria

Framed the problem as a forecasting task under experimental constraints, highlighting tradeoffs between flexibility and explanation

What I’d do next

Introduce mixed-effects models to separate within- and between-subject variability

Test regime-switching or change-point models to capture abrupt strategy shifts

Explore causal formulations linking task difficulty to reaction time adjustments
